findings.acceptance_test: NOT_RUN: parameterize one correctly hashed measured fixture with a string metrics value, a non-finite metric, an invalid UTC time, and negative RAM. Each must return fixed validation errors and no publishable paths. A list-shaped JSON receipt and a list-shaped plane value must fail through the same bounded error interface rather than escape.
findings.detail: Visible admission checks require keys and allowed labels, machine-key presence, truthy measured metrics, and a self-consistent hash. They do not enforce an object of finite numeric metrics, a valid UTC observation time, string machine/method fields, or nonnegative numeric RAM. Default JSON decoding and digest encoding also permit non-finite values. A correctly self-hashed malformed value can therefore pass these checks. Non-object JSON or unhashable labels can escape as exceptions outside the file-read handler. This is a frozen source finding, not a claim that a deployed invalid receipt exists.
findings.title: Receipt value validation is weaker than the declared admission schema

findings.acceptance_test: NOT_RUN: replace a fixture receipt after the verification call and before export. Require either an explicit integrity failure with no replacement output, or export from the exact immutable bytes already verified. The altered metrics must never be published as admitted data.
findings.detail: The chain is verified first, then the same mutable paths are reopened to check plane/time values, and measured paths are reopened again to construct output rows. A replacement between verification and either read can supply exported metrics and a receipt hash that were not the bytes admitted by the verifier. The existing initial abort-on-verifier-errors gate is a useful safeguard but does not bind these later reads.
findings.title: Sync exports bytes reopened after receipt verification

findings.acceptance_test: NOT_RUN: supply a shape-valid synthetic input containing a digest-shaped receipt label without the expected upstream admission attestation. Require rejection or an explicit unverified truth state. A changed input must also fail when its bytes no longer match the separately supplied expected verified-input digest and source pin.
findings.detail: The merge input check establishes object/list shape, count, a nonempty timestamp, expected plane, and digest-shaped unique receipt labels. It does not recompute receipt admission or require an independently authenticated expected input digest. Nevertheless the deployment payload unconditionally labels its rows measured-only. Source revisions are caller-provided syntax-valid labels. The module documents already-verified inputs as a precondition, but the enforcement of that precondition and the active publisher route remain outside this reviewed source.
findings.title: Merge truth flag assumes rather than proves verified measured inputs

findings.acceptance_test: NOT_RUN: parameterize zero repeats, negative repeats, and an empty prompt list with injected health/client fixtures. Require rejection or an explicit non-measured state before issuing generation requests. No zero-request run may emit a measured result.
findings.detail: After a successful health gate, empty prompts or zero/negative repeat counts produce an empty nested loop and an empty summary, followed by an unconditional MEASURED label. The visible CLI accepts arbitrary integer repeats and the prompt loader does not validate a nonempty prompt collection. The file contains two redacted lines, so the full request/accounting contract remains partial; these visible loop and label paths are sufficient to identify the zero-request case.
findings.title: Zero-request runs can still receive the MEASURED label

findings.acceptance_test: NOT_RUN: use a synthetic endpoint with credential-bearing URL components and injected transport exceptions containing synthetic private text. Capture result JSON, stdout, and stderr. Require fixed safe error codes and no disclosure of those components or exception contents; do not make live requests.
findings.detail: Endpoint strings are resolved directly from environment configuration, included in a blocked reason, and printed before a run. The client returns stringified or repr-form exception text, which metrics retains as errors. If configured endpoint or exception text contains credential-bearing URL components or private response data, these visible paths can disclose them. No environment values or actual credential text were read during this review; the client/runner review remains partial because accounting lines are redacted.
findings.title: Endpoint and exception text reach result or console output

findings.acceptance_test: NOT_RUN: first define the supported provider completion contract. Add a stream fixture with valid text followed by malformed JSON and an abruptly ended stream. Require an explicit invalid/partial admission state when completion is not established, while preserving the declared usage-only event compatibility.
findings.detail: Malformed JSON data events are silently skipped. A stream containing some valid text can then reach the visible successful-result path even if another data event was malformed. No explicit completed-versus-truncated stream state is visible. Existing usage-event tests intentionally allow streams without a final end marker, so completion policy needs an owner decision rather than an assumption that all providers have the same trailer contract. Redacted request/result fields make this a partial file review.
findings.title: Malformed SSE events are discarded without a partial-stream state

findings.acceptance_test: NOT_RUN: parameterize a successful sample with negative, non-finite, and boolean timing values. Require fixed rejection or explicit invalid-sample exclusion before percentile aggregation; absent valid measurements must remain unknown rather than become numeric benchmark results.
findings.detail: Successful samples are selected by their truthy success flag, and every non-null TTFT/total value is converted into percentile inputs without finite or nonnegative checks. The visible sample dataclass does not validate these timing fields. Invalid numeric samples can therefore produce invalid latency summaries. The accounting field is redacted, so no complete token-throughput type claim is made.
findings.title: Latency aggregation has no finite nonnegative value admission

findings.acceptance_test: NOT_RUN: preserve a known destination artifact, inject a write or flush failure while producing the replacement, and require an explicit failure with the original artifact bytes unchanged. A successful write should replace the destination only after the staged bytes are complete.
findings.detail: The sync tool writes directly to the destination in truncating write mode. An interrupted write or storage error can destroy a previously valid result artifact and leave a partial output. The reviewed merge tool already has a per-file atomic replacement pattern, but the sync writer does not use it. This is a source-level preservation concern, not a claim that an actual output was corrupted.
findings.title: Sync output truncates the existing artifact before writing completes
